messages:
devon: heads-up — during last scheduled capacity resize we got a burst of pages from gpu-pool-* alerts. want to re-evaluate what should page vs file a ticket. short thread for runbook/alert-rule ideas, pls chime in.

maya: saw ~27 alerts in 10m, ~5 actually actionable. noise -> ops fatigue. agree we need clearer signal rules.

juan: can we group by job pool + node role? e.g., group_key: gpu_pool/node_role/failure_type. reduces duplicates from churn.

irina: also consider cardinality cap: if alert cardinality > 50, auto-ticket at P3 instead of paging. high-cardinality flaps usually not urgent.

ops-bot: metric snapshot: auto-scaler windows at 03:00 UTC caused 23 node reboots, 18 mem-pressure alerts, 9 OOM warnings. Pager counts: 12, Tickets created: 4.

maya: propose: page if (severity="critical" AND cardinality <= 10) OR (error_type IN [kernel_panic, controller_fail]) ; else create ticket.

devon: love that. we should give examples in rule form so alert-manager can route.

sam: +1. also recommend a 5m dedupe window and a 20m suppression for scheduled resize windows. we can auto-disable paging during scheduled ops.

juan: sample prom rule I mocked:
```yaml
alert: GPUNodeMemoryPressure
expr: avg_over_time(node_memory_Bytes_used{role="gpu"}[5m]) / node_memory_Bytes_total{role="gpu"} > 0.92
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: warning
  route_group_key: '{{ gpu_pool }}:memory_pressure'
annotations:
  summary: 'GPU nodes high memory pressure ({{ $labels.instance }})'
```
Add an `if` in alertmanager to escalate to page only if `count_values("route_group_key", 5m) <= 10` and severity=critical.

irina: and for scale events specifically add label `scheduled_maint=true` so routing rules can mute/publish as tickets. Ops tooling already emits that label, we just need to propagate it.

devon: we should quantify success. target: reduce noisy pages by 70% for scheduled resize windows, keep P1 pages < 2/week for infra. track alert->incident conversion rate and mttr.

maya: small experiment: next two scheduled resizes we'll apply grouping+mute and compare page counts. create a dashboard panel: pages_per_window, distinct_alert_cardinality, tickets_created.

sam: I'll open a ticket to implement the alertmanager route changes + a small patch to translate `scheduled_maint` label from our scaler. assigning to ops-sre pair: @maya and @juan.

juan: I can own the prom rule updates and grouping keys. will push a PR with tests for dedupe logic.

devon: irina — can you run the SLA mapping doc and confirm P1/P2 mapping for infra alerts? we want consistent severity -> page mapping.

irina: yes, will update doc and ping legal if needed for SLA triggers.

ops-bot: action created: SRE-3421 "alert routing: gpu pool cardinality gating" assigned to juan, maya, due 2026-04-05.

devon: perfect. after experiment we can set a permanent policy if metrics look good. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
